subject: [RFC PATCH 0/2] mm: zsmalloc: make shrinker compaction budget-aware

reviews.author: Chris Wiseman
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the precheck for freeing zspage is a best-effort hint due to non-atomic counters, and suggested sending a patch to address this issue.

Reviewer noted that compaction still provides benefits when triggered between bursts, but wastes time running mid-swap when new writes fill up freed slots, and suggested defaulting CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER to N (or CONFIG_ZSWAP) for a couple of releases
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, it just checks if a bucket has enough wasted slots to free at
least one full page before taking the locks.  Sergey pointed out those
two counters aren't atomic together so an unlocked check is just a
best-effort hint - if you and Sergey are good with that, happy to send a
patch.

---

Compaction still helps when we trigger it between bursts (freed ~21 MB
before the swap storm and ~10 MB after).  It just wastes time running
mid-swap when new writes are filling those open slots right back up.
Defaulting CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER to N (or CONFIG_ZSWAP) for a couple
releases makes sense to me.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
Author clarifies that the precheck checks if at least one full zspage can be freed, not just a single zspage of size class.

Author acknowledged that internal compaction isn't very helpful for zsmalloc and suggested a best-effort hint approach instead of strict checking. They also proposed rechecking after acquiring the lock, but expressed doubt about getting significantly different results.
reviews.raw_body:
You meant full zspage here right? IIUC we keep the entire chain of
zpages around until the entire zspage is gone?

---

Personally I'm happy with it being a best-effort hint!

We can also recheck after we acquire the lock (but I suspect it's
unlikely we'll get radically different decision?)

Sergey, how do you feel about this?

2026-11-04.patch_summary: This patch makes the zsmalloc shrinker compaction budget-aware by adding a check to ensure that at least one page can be freed before proceeding, addressing internal fragmentation concerns and potentially reducing the need for CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER.

reviews.author: Xueyuan Chen
reviews.summary: Reviewer Xueyuan Chen noted that internal compaction isn't helpful for zsmalloc due to low internal fragmentation, and suggested making the shrinker configurable with a default value of N or CONFIG_ZSWAP
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks, Nhat and Chris, for the discussion.

If Sergey has no objections, I'd be happy to send a follow-up series
to make the shrinker configurable and add the unlocked pre-check as
Nhat suggested.

reviews.author: Sergey Senozhatsky
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested an alternative approach to implementing lockless best effort hint by introducing a ->can_compact bool flag, which would be set under the lock in zs_free(), and proposed reducing the overhead of calling zs_can_compact() on every zs_free()

Reviewer noted that the dependency on ZSWAP is problematic because it introduces a runtime knob that needs to be tied in with the zsmalloc shrinker, and requested input from the zswap developers on their preferences for this configuration.
reviews.raw_body:
Well, I guess... I don't mind the lockless best effort hint.

I suppose another way could be an introduction of ->can_compact bool flag,
which we can set under the lock in zs_free() (that's where fragmentation is
created).  zs_can_compact() doesn't seem too expensive, but calling it on
every zs_free() looks a bit bad, we sort of want to do less work in zs_free().

---

So "depends on ZSWAP" looks a bit problematic, because zswap has both
ZSWAP_SHRINKER_DEFAULT_ON (which can select CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER),
but then zswap also has module_param_named(shrinker_enabled).  So if
want to tie zsmalloc to zswap shrinker then we probably need to wire
in that run-time knob as well.  If shrinker_enabled should imply zsmalloc
shrinker (which I think it didn't so far).  zswap folks, do you have any
preferences?

reviews.author: Sergey Senozhatsky
reviews.summary:
Reviewer questioned the usefulness of internal compaction in zsmalloc, noting that it already packs objects efficiently and has minimal internal fragmentation, and suggested making CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER optional to gauge user feedback

Reviewer questioned the usefulness of internal compaction in zsmalloc, suggesting it may not be necessary due to low internal fragmentation, and proposed a temporary configuration option (CONFIG_ZSMALLOC_SHRINKER) to remove the shrinker feature if users do not complain within a couple of releases.
reviews.raw_body:
On (26/11/05 09:10), Xueyuan Chen wrote:
[..]

---

Thanks.  Sounds like you and Chris will to have "Rock-Paper-Scissors"
to determine who sends a oatch ;)  Just joking, let's first figure
out how exactly we want that zsmalloc-shrinker thing to behave wrt
zswap expectations.
